pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Scenario briefing · fictional
pages.subject: Having said that
paragraphs: Fictional study group: current weekly meeting includes 60 minutes of spoken updates. Proposal: short written update plus a 10-minute live question slot. Benefits are possible, not measured outcomes. Concerns: reading, late questions and response responsibility. A trial needs an agreed review criterion.

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What change would you propose for our weekly study-group meeting?
lines.audioText: What change would you propose for our weekly study-group meeting?
lines.translation: Que mudança você proporia para nossa reunião semanal do grupo de estudos?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I’d replace the sixty-minute status round with a short written update
lines.audioText: I’d replace the sixty-minute status round with a short written update.
lines.translation: Eu substituiria a rodada de atualização de sessenta minutos por uma atualização escrita curta

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: People repeat information we could read. We need the live time for questions
lines.audioText: People repeat information we could read. We need the live time for questions.
lines.translation: As pessoas repetem informações que poderíamos ler. Precisamos do tempo ao vivo para perguntas

questions.prompt: What part of the meeting would Ana replace?
questions.answer: Ana would replace the sixty-minute spoken status round
There would be a short written update

questions.prompt: What should live meeting time be used for?
questions.answer: Live meeting time should be used for questions

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I can see the benefit. My concern is that some people won’t read the update
lines.audioText: I can see the benefit. My concern is that some people won’t read the update.
lines.translation: Vejo o benefício. Minha preocupação é que algumas pessoas não leiam

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: That’s a fair point. Having said that, a longer meeting doesn’t guarantee attention either
lines.audioText: That’s a fair point. Having said that, a longer meeting doesn’t guarantee attention either.
lines.translation: É um ponto válido. Dito isso, uma reunião mais longa também não garante atenção

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: True. Could the update be short enough to read before a ten-minute discussion?
lines.audioText: True. Could the update be short enough to read before a ten-minute discussion?
lines.translation: Verdade. A atualização poderia ser curta o suficiente para ler antes de dez minutos de discussão?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes. We could use three headings and keep the live slot for unresolved questions
lines.audioText: Yes. We could use three headings and keep the live slot for unresolved questions.
lines.translation: Sim. Poderíamos usar três tópicos e reservar o momento ao vivo para dúvidas pendentes

questions.answer: Kim worries that some people won’t read the update

questions.prompt: Why doesn’t a longer meeting guarantee a solution?
questions.answer: A longer meeting doesn’t guarantee people’s attention
They propose an update with three headings followed by a ten-minute discussion

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What about someone who thinks of a question afterwards?
lines.audioText: What about someone who thinks of a question afterwards?
lines.translation: E quem pensar em uma pergunta depois?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: We’d need a place to ask asynchronously, and someone responsible for replies
lines.audioText: We’d need a place to ask asynchronously, and someone responsible for replies.
lines.translation: Precisaríamos de um lugar para perguntar depois e alguém responsável pelas respostas

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Then I’d support a trial, provided we check whether questions actually get answered
lines.audioText: Then I’d support a trial, provided we check whether questions actually get answered.
lines.translation: Então apoiaria um teste, desde que verifiquemos se as perguntas realmente são respondidas

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Agreed. In short, less reporting aloud, but a clearer way to get help
lines.audioText: Agreed. In short, less reporting aloud, but a clearer way to get help.
lines.translation: Combinado. Em resumo, menos leitura de atualizações em voz alta e um caminho mais claro para obter ajuda

questions.prompt: What support is needed after the live discussion?
questions.answer: They need an asynchronous question space and someone responsible for replies

questions.prompt: What condition does Kim attach to supporting the trial?
questions.answer: They must check whether questions actually get answered

questions.prompt: What is the overall purpose of the change?
questions.answer: The purpose is less reporting aloud but a clearer way to get help

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: A concern about unanswered questions. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. One group member likes the shorter meeting but is worried about asking questions after the live discussion. They can’t always join at the same time, and they don’t want their questions to disappear in a long message thread. They suggest a separate question channel, with a named person checking it each study day. Could you revise the proposal without bringing back the full sixty-minute status round? Keep its purpose—more useful time—and explain what you would change so people can still get an answer. We should agree how to review the trial before calling it a success
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. One group member likes the shorter meeting but is worried about asking questions after the live discussion. They can’t always join at the same time, and they don’t want their questions to disappear in a long message thread. They suggest a separate question channel, with a named person checking it each study day. Could you revise the proposal without bringing back the full sixty-minute status round? Keep its purpose—more useful time—and explain what you would change so people can still get an answer. We should agree how to review the trial before calling it a success.

pages.title: Make the proposal workable
pages.instruction: Spot the contradictions, then improve one proposal

items.prompt: What are they trying to decide?
items.hint: The real topic is revealed near the end
items.answer: They are choosing their coffee, and finally settle on black coffee

items.prompt: Which two suggestions contradict each other?
items.answer: They propose coffee that is both extremely hot and frozen solid

items.prompt: What does “no bad ideas” mean to them?
items.hint: Notice what happens when someone suggests ice cream
items.answer: They interpret the rule as allowing only good suggestions and reject the ice-cream idea

items.prompt: How would you acknowledge one objection and improve the proposal?
items.hint: Recognise the concern, then qualify your proposal
items.answer: Example: That is a fair point. Having said that, let us keep the coffee simple and choose one temperature
